item.title: [World news | The Guardian] Knickers in a twist: why M&S selling crotchless underwear isn’t as outrageous as it seems
item.description:
Some have called it ‘S&M’, but partnership with Ann Summers is less a scandal than another step in a century of evolving underwear trends, experts say

The news that Marks & Spencer is selling Ann Summers crotchless knickers on their website has been greeted – as might be expected – with outrage online, being described as everything from “tawdry” to “S & M”.

But it could be this is just the latest evolution in what the UK’s biggest underwear retailer has available for the smalls drawer. In recent years, the store has sold vastly different options through its own products, ranging from full-brief knickers to thongs, period knickers and those that can be used by women who wear stomas. The introduction of other brands in clothing came five years ago, with underwear included. Ann Summers – which is selling bras and chemises as well as knickers on the M&S website – lines up alongside lingerie brands including Pour Moi and Calvin Klein.

Iran’s foreign ministry has warned Gulf states against allowing the US and Israel to use their territory to carry out attacks on Iran.

In a statement circulated via the country's Fars news agency, the foreign ministry said: “The governments of the region have a legal, religious, and moral duty to prevent the United States and the Zionist regime from using their territory and facilities to attack Iran.”

The statement comes after US President Donald Trump warned on Friday that the US would hit Iran "very hard" with a new wave of attacks in the coming days.

item.description:
Iraqi premier al-Zaydi announces 'deterrent measures' against playing role in regional hostilities

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaydi has announced "deterrent measures" to prevent attacks on "neighbouring countries" coming from within Iraqi territory, following an emergency meeting with domestic security forces late Saturday.  

The announcement, which did not provide further detail on the planned measures, comes after the Iraq-based Popular Mobilisation Forces paramilitary launched drone attacks at Saudi energy infrastructure earlier this week, prompting US and Saudi retaliatory strikes. The PMF paramilitary, which is dominated by pro-Iranian Shia factions, said that over 20 of its fighters were killed in the strikes. 

Iraq also found itself in the crosshairs of the US-Israeli war on Iran earlier this a wave of attacks this week on Iranian Kurdish groups based in Iraqi territory, which that have been widely attributed to Iran.

A statement provided by al-Zaydi's office on Saturday said that the emergency meeting "reaffirmed the readiness of the Armed Forces to thwart any attempt targeting neighboring countries within our regional environment."

It added that the Iraqi government had was committed "to preventing Iraqi territory from being used as a launching point or passageway for attacks against brotherly or friendly countries, in fulfillment of its responsibility to safeguard national sovereignty and uphold the principles of good neighborliness and international law.”

Authorities in Gaza have said that civil defence teams recovered the remains of 112 more people from rubble in the Sabra neighbourhood of Gaza City after 136 hours of digging, much of it by hand.

The recovered remains included 40 children, 38 women and seven people with physical disabilities, AFP reported.

The International Committee of the Red Cross said it supported the nearly two-week operation. Its Gaza spokesperson, Amani Al-Naouq, said thousands of families had spent more than two and a half years waiting to recover the remains of loved ones and described the search for missing people as a critical humanitarian issue, according to AFP.

Colonel Mohammed Abu Dan, who is overseeing the site for Gaza's civil defence agency, said crews believe another 157 bodies remain buried beneath the rubble and that search efforts are continuing despite the difficult conditions.

The statement said the US was “persisting in its bad faith regarding the implementation of the agreement to end the war” through “brutal attacks on various regions of the country, intensified economic pressure, and illegal threats”.

The ministry hailed “the unparalleled efforts of our nation’s glorious armed forces in the powerful defence of Iran’s sovereignty” and paid tribute to the “noble spirit of our martyred leader and all those who sacrificed their lives for Iran’s independence and honour”.

The ministry said it reaffirmed the country’s resolve to “continue the path of resistance and steadfastness until the complete elimination of the enemies’ malice”.

item.description:
Pezeshkian recalls Haniyeh assassination, hails Iranians as 'real heroes'

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian marked two years in office by recalling the killing of Hamas political chief Ismail Haniyeh and praising the Iranian people's resilience through “relentless hostility”.

In a statement carried by IRNA, Pezeshkian said his presidency began under the shadow of tragedy, noting that "the beginning of my administration coincided with the assassination of our dear guest by the Zionist regime."

Haniyeh was assassinated in Tehran on 31 July 2024, hours after attending Pezeshkian's inauguration, where delegations from more than 70 countries were present. 

Pezeshkian's presidency has since been marked by what he called "wars, pressure, and relentless hostility" against Iran, including a foreign-backed coup attempt and two US-Israeli wars.

"Throughout all these difficult days, the real heroes were the people," he said, adding that Iranians "will shape the future of Iran."

Iran and "other Middle Eastern Countries" asked for time to complete a deal that would lead to "the Immediate, Complete and Total" reopening of the Strait and "an end to Iran's nuclear threat," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.

Israel "joins me in this commitment," Trump wrote.

item.description:
Two children among eight Palestinians killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza

Overnight Israeli strikes on Gaza killed at least eight people, including two children, despite Hamas saying it agreed to the latest stage of a deal to end the war.

Gaza civil defence officials said in one attack near the central Gaza Strip, a man and his wife were killed and several others were wounded when an Israeli military helicopter struck an apartment, AFP reported.

An elderly man and a child were killed in another attack on an apartment west of Gaza City, and three people, including a child, were targeted when a strike hit another apartment northwest of Khan Younis in the southern Gaza Strip.

Authorities reported earlier Saturday that eight other people had been killed in strikes that damaged a hospital's medical supplies and targeted a rooftop.

In March, Senegal doubled the maximum prison sentence for gay sex to 10 years and criminalised the “promotion” of homosexuality. Niger criminalised “sexual relations with a person of the same sex” in February, the first time same-sex intimacy had been outlawed in the country.

item.description:
Former Israeli prime minister vows to declare Qatar ‘enemy’ if elected

Former prime minister Naftali Bennett has vowed to declare Qatar as an “enemy” if elected into government later this year, saying “it is unforgivable” that this is not already the case.

In an interview with Channel 12, Bennett described Qatar as “more dangerous” to Israel at the moment than Iran.

 “With Iran, everyone knows that [it says], ‘We’ll destroy Israel.’” But Qatar, he said, “funded the Nukhba terrorists of October 7 [2023]… Qatar operates Al Jazeera, which is the most poisonous cancer hurting us.”

“Qatar reaches places of influence in American universities… And most importantly, [it has access] to the most sacred place for the security of Israel — that is the office of the prime minister of Israel,” he said.

"Qatar works against us and poisons us from within,” Bennett said, fuming that Israel does not define Qatar as an enemy state.

Seconds later a Ukrainian drone roared into a mauve sky. It jerked upwards at a 45-degree angle, orange flames fizzing, and then motored serenely onwards. Saudi Arabia expressed concern over US President Donald Trump's plans for massive strikes against Iran and sought clarity on the proposed course of action, US outlet Axios reported.
